original_question: Let F1, ..., Fs be homogeneous forms of degree d in variables y1, ..., yn, let x1, ..., xs be new variables, and consider the Artinian Gorenstein algebra whose Macaulay inverse system is generated by sum_i x_i^e F_i. Determine, for general values of e and for specific choices of the forms F_i, when this Gorenstein algebra has the weak Lefschetz property and when it has the strong Lefschetz property.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right family of Artinian Gorenstein algebras: those with Macaulay dual generator sum_{i=1}^s x_i^e F_i, where the F_i are homogeneous forms of common degree d in the y-variables and x_1,...,x_s are new variables. It also correctly recognizes that the paper asks about both the weak and strong Lefschetz properties for this family, and that the dependence on the exponent e and on the choice of the forms F_i is central to the problem.
missing_details: The paper works in Section 4 over a field K of characteristic 0, and that ambient hypothesis should be stated explicitly.

The algebra should be presented as the standard graded Artinian Gorenstein quotient A_e = K[X_1,...,X_s,Y_1,...,Y_n]/Ann(G_e), with G_e = sum_{i=1}^s x_i^e F_i, rather than only informally as an algebra whose inverse system is generated by that form.
The operator convention should be made explicit: X_i and Y_j act as differential operators d/dx_i and d/dy_j on the dual polynomial ring K[x_1,...,x_s,y_1,...,y_n].
The exponent e should be quantified as an integer e >= 1.
It should be stated explicitly that each F_i lies in K[y_1,...,y_n]_d, so all F_i have the same degree d.
The grading should be made explicit: all variables have degree 1, so G_e is homogeneous of degree d+e and A_e is standard graded.

For the question to be stand-alone, WLP and SLP should be defined: existence of a linear form ell in degree 1 such that multiplication by ell, respectively by ell^k for all k >= 1, has maximal rank in every degree.

The nearby context matters: for e = 1 this construction is presented as the Nagata idealization of the canonical module of an Artinian level algebra with inverse system <F_1,...,F_s>, while the paper then considers the higher-order variant with x_i^e.

To match the paper sharply, the known partial results from the same paragraph should be acknowledged: WLP is already reported for all choices of F_i when e >= d, while for e < d the paper says there are both WLP and non-WLP examples; thus the real unresolved issue is the precise classification, especially for e < d and for SLP.
No separate nilpotency hypothesis is imposed in the paper; Artinian-ness is built into the quotient construction, so that should be stated directly rather than left implicit.
refined_question: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let F_1,...,F_s be homogeneous forms of common degree d in K[y_1,...,y_n], let x_1,...,x_s be new variables, and for an integer e >= 1 set G_e = sum_{i=1}^s x_i^e F_i in K[x_1,...,x_s,y_1,...,y_n]. Let A_e := K[X_1,...,X_s,Y_1,...,Y_n]/Ann(G_e), where X_i = d/dx_i and Y_j = d/dy_j act by differentiation on G_e, so that A_e is the standard graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra with Macaulay dual generator G_e. Determine for which integers e and which choices of F_1,...,F_s the algebra A_e has the weak Lefschetz property and for which it has the strong Lefschetz property; that is, determine when there exists a linear form ell in (A_e)_1 such that multiplication by ell, respectively by ell^k for every k >= 1, has maximal rank in every degree. In particular, classify the unresolved range e < d, since the paper records that WLP already holds for all F_i when e >= d.
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's Nagata-idealization problem. In Section 4, after fixing the characteristic-0 setup for that section, the authors introduce Nagata idealizations via Macaulay inverse systems: starting from an Artinian level algebra with inverse system <F_1,...,F_s>, one gets a Gorenstein algebra with inverse system <sum x_i F_i>, where the F_i are homogeneous of degree d in y_1,...,y_n and the x_i are new variables. The same paragraph immediately says that they also studied the generalized construction with dual generator sum x_i^e F_i, reports the partial results e >= d implies WLP for any forms F_i and e < d admits both WLP and non-WLP examples, and then states Problem 4.7: determine whether the Gorenstein algebra given by sum x_i^e F_i has the WLP and/or the SLP. So your draft is very close, but to be fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper it needs the ambient field, the quotient-by-annihilator construction, the differential-operator convention, the quantifier e >= 1, the standard grading, and the explicit definitions of WLP/SLP.
